reason: Start building the heart by joining its muscle to the supporting framework.
expectation: I expect a heart-wall structure supported by the framework, though it may still need lining and partitions.

alternatives.reason: Building the pulmonary route is also necessary, but I want to start with the heart.

effect: The heart framework has slots for lining, septa and valves; the thicker left wall reflects the higher-pressure body circuit.
reaction: The pressure difference gives the unequal wall thickness a clear purpose, although the picture description mixes unfinished and completed views.
reason: Add the lining to the open chamber interiors as the next heart component.
expectation: The heart chambers will gain a smooth inner lining, with septa and valves still to add.

alternatives.reason: The partitions are also needed, but lining the chambers seems a natural next step.

effect: The lining is fitted; the septa and valves remain to be added.
reaction: A straightforward fitting, with no further detail about the lining.
reason: Add the septa to divide the right and left sides of the heart.
expectation: The heart will gain its partitions, leaving the valves to be fitted.

alternatives.reason: The valves are also needed, but I would first separate the chambers.

effect: The septa are fitted, leaving the valves as the remaining heart component.
reaction: Another straightforward fitting without additional detail.
reason: Fit the valves to complete the heart's listed components.
expectation: The heart will gain valves at the chamber and artery openings, ready for connection to the vessel routes.

alternatives.reason: The pulmonary route is also needed, but I want to finish the heart first.

effect: The valves are fitted, completing the heart's listed components; the vessel routes remain to be connected.
reaction: The fitting is straightforward, though it doesn't yet show how the valves respond to pressure.
reason: Build the pulmonary vessel route so it can eventually connect the heart to the lungs.
expectation: The pulmonary arteries and veins will be joined by the capillary mesh, forming a route through the lungs.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the systemic network is also needed, but I want to assemble the pulmonary route first.

effect: The pulmonary arteries, capillaries and veins now form a connected route ready to join the heart.
reaction: The connection is clear, though the description adds little about lung exchange.
reason: Connect the newly assembled pulmonary route to the heart.
expectation: The pulmonary vessels will attach to the heart, leaving the systemic route and blood to be connected.

alternatives.reason: The systemic route also needs connection, but the pulmonary network is already assembled.

effect: The pulmonary loop is connected, with the systemic openings still free.
reaction: The remaining openings make the next connection clear.
reason: Connect the systemic network; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The systemic vessels will join the heart, completing both vessel routes; blood may still need to be added.

effect: Both vessel routes now form one closed circuit through the heart twice; blood still needs to be added.
reaction: The clarification that arteries carry blood away from the heart regardless of oxygen level is useful.
reason: Add blood to the connected circulation; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: Blood will enter the double circulation, completing the goal of joining blood, heart and vessel routes.
